All 4 phases are complete. Here's a summary of the analysis:

## Results

**Outputs written:**
- `case-studies/crossbeam-deque/modeling-brief.md` — Handoff document for spec generation
- `case-studies/crossbeam-deque/analysis-report.md` — Detailed audit trail

## Coverage Statistics
- 75 commits analyzed (10 bug-fix commits identified)
- 42+ GitHub issues read in full with comments
- 30+ PRs read in detail
- 1 CVE (CVE-2021-32810)
- All 2,233 lines of `deque.rs` read and analyzed
- All 37 unsafe blocks audited
- All 6 CAS sites checked for buffer re-check consistency
- All atomic orderings verified against Le et al. PPoPP 2013

## 5 Bug Families Identified

| # | Family | Priority | Key Finding |
|---|--------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | **Steal-Resize Buffer Race** | HIGH | CVE-2021-32810 + 1 new finding (missing buffer re-check at line 1083) |
| 2 | **Torn Read / Memory Model UB** | MEDIUM | Volatile read/write remains formally UB (documented, unfixed) |
| 3 | **Epoch-Deque Lifecycle Coupling** | MEDIUM | M1 segfault (#869) root cause still unknown |
| 4 | **FIFO Pop Rollback Atomicity** | LOW | Transient false-empty window, no historical bugs |
| 5 | **Injector Obstruction-Freedom** | LOW | Stalled pusher blocks all stealers |

## Key New Finding

**DA-1**: `deque.rs:1083-1087` — The LIFO path in `steal_batch_with_limit_and_pop` is the **only** CAS site (out of 6) that lacks the buffer re-check added for the CVE-2021-32810 fix. Safe in practice due to epoch protection, but inconsistent with the defense-in-depth pattern applied everywhere else. Model checking can verify whether this omission is exploitable.
